decisions.reason: The standalone USB source remains a 3.3V LDO used when the power board is disconnected; changing the separate DCDC1 source to 3.4V for diode-drop compensation does not alter this requirement.
The monitored rails, INA219 placement after the Schottky diodes, and downstream measurement coverage remain unchanged by the upstream DCDC1 voltage adjustment.
AXP2101 remains the normal-operation power source and the delivered system rail remains 3.3V; the DCDC1 configuration detail is already owned by the source requirement.
The same message independently introduces the panel power-button interface, but the DCDC1 voltage change does not modify any button connector or switching behavior.
The source changes DCDC1 and its downstream 3.3V rail compensation, not the MT3608-based software-switched 5V rail.
The charge-status LED, connector, and resistor requirements are unaffected by the DCDC1 output-voltage adjustment.
The battery connector family, pin count, functions, and unresolved pin order are unaffected by DCDC1 diode-drop compensation.
The source does not change battery overcharge, overdischarge, thermal sensing, or protection behavior.
The DCDC1 voltage configuration has no entailed effect on the power-board TVS ESD protection requirement.
The three-board architecture and main-board role remain unchanged; adjusting an upstream supply to preserve the existing 3.3V rail does not change board responsibilities.
The source does not change ESP32 clocking, sleep policy, power-state entry conditions, or wake sources.

The interboard connectors continue to distribute a regulated 3.3V rail; the upstream 3.4V setting compensates for the Schottky drop and does not change connector topology, pinout, or delivered rail designation.
